facts_from_discussion: Petitioner separated from service with Rockwell (in 1987) and with Northrop Grumman (in 1999) before he attained age 55; he was 46 years old in 2002.
The Boeing lump-sum distribution was from petitioner's Rockwell pension plan, a qualified retirement plan.

Petitioners concede there is no general hardship exception, and they do not argue that any statutory exception other than the age-55 separation-from-service exception of sec. 72(t)(2)(A)(v) applies to the Boeing distribution.
Petitioners contend that it suffices that the participant has attained age 55 and is separated from service, regardless of the age at separation.
notes: Footnote 2's statement that the $7,080 Northrop Grumman distribution falls within the SEPP exception is itself a legal conclusion, but the case treats it as undisputed; kept as a neutral description so the encoder knows that distribution is not in issue.
